paper.title: Paenibacillus hubeiensis sp. nov.: A Novel Selenium-Resistant Bacterium Isolated from the Rhizosphere of Galinsoga parviflora in a Selenium-Rich Region of Enshi, Hubei Province
paper.licenseScope: Article text and original article material under the article's stated CC BY 4.0 license; third-party material may have separate terms. Claims here are paraphrases with attribution.

morphology.text: The type strain ES5-4T is described as Gram-positive, motile, aerobic and rod-shaped. The authors also report milky, circular, moist, smooth colonies after three days on TSA at 28 °C.
morphology.locator: Species description, section ‘Description of Paenibacillus hubeiensis sp. nov.’; type strain ES5-4T
morphology.scope: The cultured type strain and the conditions stated in the species description.
morphology.gap: This is a bounded type-strain description, not a survey of morphology across populations, developmental states or environmental conditions.

lifeHistory.gap: The cited taxonomic treatment is not a life-history study. Reproductive, developmental, behavioral and lifespan claims were not assessed.

ecology.text: The type strain was isolated from the rhizosphere of Galinsoga parviflora in a selenium-rich ore area of Enshi, Hubei Province, China. The paper reports laboratory tolerance of selenite up to 5000 mg/L; that assay result is not evidence of a field threshold or ecological function.
ecology.locator: Abstract; species description and strain isolation account
ecology.scope: One cultured type strain and the paper's stated collection context; the selenite value is an in-vitro assay result.
ecology.gap: No population ecology, interaction network, abundance, field exposure distribution or complete habitat survey was assessed.

evolution.text: The authors place ES5-4T within Paenibacillus using 16S rRNA and a bac120 phylogenomic tree, and report ANI and dDDH values below their stated species-level cutoffs against close type strains. This records the authors' taxonomic evidence, not a comprehensive or independently reviewed species-tree conclusion.
evolution.locator: Abstract; phylogenetic and genomic comparison sections; bac120 tree and ANI/dDDH results
evolution.scope: The strains, markers, genome comparisons and methods analyzed in this 2025 paper.
evolution.gap: Alternative taxon sampling, later revisions, gene-tree discordance and independent phylogenomic review were not assessed.

distribution.text: The paper reports the type strain from the Galinsoga parviflora rhizosphere in the selenium-rich ore area of Enshi, Hubei Province, China.
distribution.scope: The reported type-strain collection locality only; this is not a global range claim.
distribution.gap: No additional localities, native or introduced range, georeferenced boundary or sampling completeness were established.

fossil.gap: No paleontological or fossil database search was conducted; no fossil-presence or fossil-absence conclusion is made.

conservation.gap: No conservation assessment or current formal Red List record was assessed.

paper.title: Phenotypic and Genomic Characterization of a Sulfate-Reducing Bacterium Pseudodesulfovibrio methanolicus sp. nov. Isolated from a Petroleum Reservoir in Russia
paper.licenseScope: OpenAlex reports the item-level work license as CC BY; MDPI article landing page and article record identify the open-access paper. Claims here are paraphrases with attribution; third-party material may have separate terms.

morphology.text: The type strain 5S69T is reported as Gram-negative, strictly anaerobic, non-spore-forming, and straight or slightly curved rods measuring 0.35–0.45 × 1.0–2.0 μm; cells are motile by a single polar flagellum.
morphology.scope: The cultured type strain in the exponential-growth phase under study conditions.
morphology.gap: These observations do not characterize population variation or all growth phases and environments.

lifeHistory.gap: No life-history study or systematic search was performed; reproduction, development, behavior and lifespan are not characterized.

ecology.text: The authors isolated strain 5S69T from injection water collected at the Vostochno-Anzirskoe oil field in Tatarstan, Russia, and characterize it as sulfate-reducing. These observations do not establish a measured field-scale role in carbon or sulfur cycling.
ecology.locator: Abstract; sections 3.1 and 4; strain isolation context
ecology.scope: The single cultured type strain and the sampled oil-field water described in the article.
ecology.gap: No in-situ abundance, activity rate, interaction network or reservoir-wide survey was assessed.

evolution.text: The study uses 16S rRNA, 120 conserved single-copy proteins and genomic relatedness indices to support placement of 5S69T as a distinct Pseudodesulfovibrio species. It reports this as the authors' taxonomic conclusion.
evolution.locator: Abstract; phylogenetic and genomic index analyses; conclusions
evolution.scope: The type strain and comparator strains in the 2024 study.
evolution.gap: Alternative taxon sampling, later nomenclatural changes and independent phylogenomic review were not assessed.

distribution.text: The paper reports the type strain from injection water collected at the Vostochno-Anzirskoe oil field, Tatarstan, Russia.
distribution.scope: One reported collection locality only; no wider range is implied.
distribution.gap: No further localities, global range, georeferenced boundary or sampling completeness were assessed.

fossil.gap: No fossil or paleontological literature/database search was performed; no fossil-presence or fossil-absence conclusion is made.

conservation.gap: No conservation assessment or current formal Red List record was assessed.

morphology.text: The article provides scanning and transmission electron micrographs of strain 9FUS-T cells, including a flagellum and an ultrathin section. The microscopy caption states that the strain was grown in lactate/sulfate medium for seven days at 25 C.

ecology.text: Strain 9FUS-T was isolated from formation water at the Karazhanbas oil field in Kazakhstan and characterized as sulfate-reducing. The article discusses petroleum-industry sulfidogenesis; it does not measure field-scale activity of the species.
